also: shut up the hens for the night

terms.comment: Columella’s word (8.3.1) and Pliny’s (17.51), the noun of gallīnārius; Traupman has it too.

phrases.english: Do you want to see the hens in the hen-house?
It’s light now; let’s let the hens out.

phrases.latin: Advesperāscit; gallīnās inclūde, nē vulpēs veniat.
phrases.english: It’s getting dark; shut the hens in, so the fox doesn’t come.

phrases.latin: Gallīna post prīmam ēmittī et ante hōram diēī ūndecimam claudī dēbet
phrases.english: A hen should be let out after the first hour and shut in before the eleventh hour of the day

phrases.latin: Sed cūrandum erit ut semper noctibus claudantur, quō tūtius avēs maneant.
phrases.english: But care must be taken that they are always shut in at night, so that the birds stay safer.

sources: Lewis & Short: gallinarius
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 141, 290.
